candidates.title: Keep training streaks visible

demandEvidence.chore: Maintain a visible training streak and points record to support motivation.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Added a system of streaks and points to motivate me train and it has become part of my daily routine.

ease.reason: A beginner can test a simple manual log, but the post does not specify trainer data access or a repeatable workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent fitness coaches may pay for motivation tracking; the post reports one person's routine, not buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can award points from manually entered sessions; data capture and sustained motivation remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A rule can update a supplied session log, but a person must enter workouts and decide whether the reward system is useful.

evidence.reason: The post says streaks and points became part of a daily training routine, but gives no repeated buyer evidence or measured effect.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable weekly training streak and points summary from manually supplied session entries.
experimentPlan.trigger: A person enters or pastes a new training session.
steps: Validate each entry has a date and activity label.
Apply the proposed points rule to the supplied session.
Update a streak count using the dates in the test log.
Produce a weekly summary and flag gaps for review.
Ask a coach or test user to inspect whether the rules are useful.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed fictional log, compare every awarded point and streak count with a hand-calculated expected summary.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The user supplies and corrects all session records; a person chooses the scoring rule and reviews whether it encourages safe training. No workout advice is produced.
unverified: Whether users sustain training from points
Whether a coach or other buyer would pay

candidates.reason: Below six: a proposed manual training log is testable, but the single self-reported routine does not establish a professional buyer or recurring demand.

candidates.title: Save and resume research sessions

demandEvidence.chore: Save a research session so a person can resume it later or export and share its record.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Research Trails - An .MD record of a research session you can jump in and out of, export and share.

ease.reason: A beginner can prototype a session record using supplied notes, but no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent research consultants may pay for session continuity; this launch excerpt establishes no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can store and export operator-supplied notes, while reliable resume state and collaboration remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A tool can format and retrieve supplied session records, but a person must capture notes and verify the resumed context.

evidence.reason: The excerpt describes a research-session record that can be resumed, exported and shared, but provides no use frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A dated Markdown research-session record that a person can reopen and export.
experimentPlan.trigger: A researcher starts a session or asks to resume a saved one.
steps: Collect the title, notes and next-step note from the operator.
Format them into a dated Markdown record.
Save the record under a manually chosen session label.
Reopen the selected record and display its notes and next step.
Export the record for a person to inspect and share.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Save a fictional session, reopen it by its label, and verify the exported text contains all supplied notes and the next-step field.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The researcher supplies, names and checks the notes; this test does not crawl sources, establish factual accuracy, or prove shared editing.
unverified: Whether session identity remains reliable across a real research project
Whether export and sharing work across intended tools
Whether research professionals have recurring need or willingness to pay

candidates.reason: Below six: the excerpt names a useful session-record workflow, but this launch description does not establish independent demand, frequency, or implementation capabilities.

candidates.title: Draft reflection prompts from a conversation

demandEvidence.chore: Review a conversation and identify small alternative moves that could surface hidden assumptions.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Basically, the tool reframes conversations and tries to find the smallest moves the user COULD have made to have surfaced unknown assumptions

ease.reason: A student can test prompts on fictional conversation text, but the source gives no method or implementation support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent facilitators may pay for reflection aids; this product excerpt does not establish their demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week text-only prototype is bounded, but useful alternative moves and assumption detection need human evaluation.

autonomy.reason: The system could draft prompts from supplied text, while a person must judge context, fairness, and whether suggestions are appropriate.

evidence.reason: The excerpt describes reframing conversations to surface assumptions, but gives no evaluation criteria, recurring use, or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A short review memo listing possible assumptions and alternative questions from supplied conversation text.
experimentPlan.trigger: A facilitator pastes a conversation excerpt and its stated goal.
steps: Check that the supplied text and goal are present.
Draft possible assumptions as questions, not conclusions.
Suggest small alternative questions tied to exact supplied passages.
Mark suggestions that lack a clear text basis.
Return the memo for a facilitator to review or discard.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional transcripts with a hand-written answer key, verify each suggested question points to a supplied passage and unsupported suggestions are marked.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A facilitator supplies the excerpt and goal, reviews every interpretation, and decides what to ask; the tool must not judge participants or infer personal traits.
unverified: Whether prompts reliably surface useful assumptions
Whether facilitators have a repeated paid need
Any documented method or validated capability

candidates.reason: Below six: a reflection memo can be tested on synthetic text, but the excerpt does not define a reliable method, recurring professional need, or buyer.
